title: Preserve human-wait state in direct procedure execution
description:
## Problem

A directly executed Tactus procedure can persist its checkpoint and enter a human-approval boundary, but the outer task runner subsequently records the procedure as failed while retaining a pending message ID. This makes a resumable pause appear terminal and blocks supported credential-free resume validation.

## Expected behavior

Given a local procedure reaches a human-interaction boundary
When the runtime returns control after persisting the pending request
Then the procedure and task remain in a resumable waiting state
And no failure status is written
And all persisted artifacts remain available through the application-authorized storage path.

## Acceptance

- An executable behavior test reproduces the incorrect terminal failure first.
- The direct runner preserves the waiting state without treating it as success or failure.
- Resume consumes the response and completes from persisted checkpoints.
- No authentication or storage fallback is introduced.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Kickoff: live Cognito sandbox acceptance on combined validation SHA 391189e09 persisted code, state, dashboard state, Lua state, and checkpoints through signed artifact tickets with AWS credentials and API keys absent. The inner runtime created a pending approval and stored waitingOnMessageId, but the outer runner wrote FAILED. Reproducing this in a focused behavior test before the minimal fix.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Milestone: the behavior-first test is green. Direct execution now recognizes persisted WAITING_FOR_HUMAN state, preserves the pending message identifier, and does not fail Task stages.
